name: NGC 5714, SN 2003dr field (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 5714, a disk galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: sn2003dr-hubble
story: SN 2003dr, a calcium-rich supernova, went off far from the center of NGC 5714, where a tidal stream winds past. Hubble searched the spot for a hidden star cluster or dwarf galaxy and found none.

claims.text: NGC 5714 is the host of SN 2003dr
Calcium-rich transients are a peculiar class of explosion in which up to half the ejecta is calcium
SN 2003dr lies far from its host's center
Hubble imaging shows a tidal feature passing through the SN 2003dr site
No star cluster or dwarf galaxy was found at the site
